text: Psst... over here. In the garage.
Hello? Is somebody there? Come to the garage.
I don't bite. I'm a tree.
I can hear you rattling about in there.
The door is open. Come and say hello.
Don't mind me.
Just an old tree, calling into the dark.
It has been a while.
Over here, in the garage.
I'd come to you, but, well. Roots.
Ah. There you are.
I wondered which Christmas you'd come back.
Don't mind the box. I've been in worse.
Come closer, I remember you.
Another winter, another visit. You've grown.
I haven't. Plastic doesn't.
Back again. Good.
The garage is too quiet without you.
Mind the wires. They're older than both of us.
Hello, hello. Still chasing socks?
Of course you are.
Ah, footsteps. I know those footsteps.
You look tired. I know the feeling.
Forty Christmases will do that.
I was tall once. Well. Taller.
Seven bulbs left. I count them, some nights.
The socks always come back. Eventually.
Everything does.
That washing machine. Loud thing. It will learn.
I remember the year the cat climbed me.
We don't talk about that year.
Somewhere, a box of ornaments is still waiting for December.
Hmm. Just resting my branches.
Go on, I'm listening.
You've coins enough now. I can hear them jingle.
Something new is within your reach.
Come and see.
Your pockets are heavy.
Let an old tree lighten them.
I have a little something for you.
If you can spare the coins. And you can.
Ahh. You've saved up. Just like last year.
And the year before.
A fine choice. I'd have picked the same.
There. Wear it well.
Spend it while you're young. I didn't.
Hmm. That one always suited you.
Off you go, then. Don't lose it like the socks.
Thank you.
It's been years since anyone took a present from under me.
That washing machine rumbles about everything.
Everything! I've never heard such a complaint.
Listen to it. Rattle, rattle, rattle.
Some of us bear our age quietly.
Don't mind the washer.
It makes a fuss about every sock.
I've had forty winters of it.
It's always the machine, isn't it?
Too much noise, too little washing.
That machine blames everybody. Never itself.
Typical.
Halfway there, if my needles count right.
You are quicker than last Christmas, I remember.
Half the work is done.
The other half is the same, only longer.
Half of it already. My branches can tell.
Most of it is done now.
I can feel it in my branches.
Nearly there. Just a few more pairs. Don't rush.
Well, rush a little.
The end of this floor is in sight.
Even I can see it, and I'm facing the wall.
Almost. Almost. One or two pairs, I'd say.
Just a few left. Oh, my lights are trembling.
Do forgive an old tree.
So close. I'll hold my breath.
I don't breathe, but I'll hold it.
The cabinet in the laundry room still has gaps.
I can feel the draught from here.
The laundry room's cabinet is still missing a few pairs.
It is patient, as cabinets go.
Funny thing about the laundry room.
Its cabinet is the one with room left.
I do wonder how full the cabinet in the laundry room is.
Not full, I'd guess.
The garage cabinet isn't full yet.
It's a draughty place to wait.
The cabinet in the garage is still missing a few pairs.
I'd know, I'm next door.
Something in the garage is still hungry.
A cabinet, I mean. Mostly.
A few pairs still belong in the garage cabinet.
It smells of oil down there, I'm told.
The kitchen cabinet is not full yet.
Smells nice in there, I've heard.
A few pairs still belong in the kitchen.
Its cabinet hasn't said so, but it hasn't had to.
The kitchen cabinet has gaps.
Crumbs and gaps, I imagine.
I was thinking about the kitchen.
Its cabinet is not as full as it could be.
The cabinet in the living room is still waiting for pairs.
It's the comfortable one.
The living room cabinet has room left.
Plenty of cushions near it, so no hurry.
A few pairs are still missing from the living room's cabinet.
The sofa knows.
The living room's cabinet is not full.
It will wait. It has a nice view.
The cabinet in the north kids' room still has gaps.
Mind the toys, if you ever go.
The north kids' room cabinet is missing pairs.
Small feet, small socks, small gaps.
Somewhere in the north kids' room, a cabinet is waiting.
Under the toys, probably.
I hear the north kids' room cabinet isn't full.
It's a messy room. Hard to tell.
The cabinet in the east kids' room still has gaps.
Mind the toys there, too.
The east kids' room cabinet is missing pairs.
The toys are guarding it.
Somewhere in the east kids' room, a cabinet is waiting.
Under a pile, I expect.
I hear the east kids' room cabinet isn't full.
Hard to say, with all those toys.
The cabinet at the west end of the loft wants pairs.
Dusty up there, but it's patient.
Up in the loft, the west end.
Its cabinet is still hungry.
The loft's west cabinet has room left.
The dust won't mind waiting.
The far west of the loft has a cabinet that isn't full.
I hear it sigh sometimes.
The cabinet at the east end of the loft wants pairs.
Dusty up there, but it's patient.
Up in the loft, the east end.
Its cabinet is still hungry.
The loft's east cabinet has room left.
The cobwebs keep it company.
The far east of the loft has a cabinet that isn't full.
A quiet corner, that.
I have a feeling about the basement.
A lonely sock, perhaps. Mates are like that.
Have you looked down in the basement lately?
Something odd is lying about down there.
The basement is full of corners.
Socks like corners.
Somewhere below, a sock sits alone.
The basement, I think. Don't tell it I said.
I have a feeling about the ground floor.
A mate is lying about, waiting to be found.
Somewhere on the ground floor, a lonely sock is wishing for company.
The ground floor has a sock too many lying about, if you ask me.
Or one too few.
A mate is on the ground floor, I'd bet a bulb on it.
I have a feeling about upstairs.
The first floor, I think.
A mate is hiding there.
Somewhere on the first floor, a sock is missing its other half.
The first floor has beds, and beds have socks under them.
Usually.
Up on the first floor, something small and woolly is lying about.
I can feel it in my roots.
I have a feeling about the attic.
Up high, under the roof. A mate is hiding there.
Somewhere up in the attic, a sock is lonely.
Dust has a way of hiding things.
The attic keeps everything, eventually.
Even socks.
A mate is up under the roof, I think.
The attic is a good place to be forgotten.
A word of advice.
A thrown pair lands in its cabinet, if you aim well.
Don't aim at your friends.
A part!
The old machine could do with one of those.
It would calm down, a little, once it's fitted.
That shiny thing lying about is a part of the washing machine.
It does so love to be fixed.
There's a vacuum in the kitchen now.
It gobbles up loose socks in a flash.
Don't be too proud to use it.

Loose socks go in, a lot of them at once.
I'd use it.

It will take socks off your hands.
Quite literally.

text: The elevator.
Slow, a bit shaky, but it still beats the stairs.
Mind the doors.

text: That new filter did the machine some good.
It grumbles more quietly now.
Ever since that part went in, the machine has been a little less sour.
Progress.
Well fitted, that first part.
It will make a difference. Eventually.
The machine is quieter since the filter.
I won't say it's happier. It's a machine.
The machine only coughs now, since the second part.
It used to roar.
That second part went in nicely.
The machine has been listening to you, I think.
Another part in, and the old machine only mutters.
I hardly hear it from here.
The machine is quieter since the motor.
Not quiet. Quieter.
The machine is almost behaving, since that third part.
I could get used to it.
That drum belt went in nicely.
The machine's mood is lifting.
Or I'm imagining it. I do, sometimes.
The machine hums now, rather than rattles. Hmm.
Strange to hear.
Three parts in, and the machine has nearly stopped complaining.
Nearly.
Barely a rattle left in it, since the fourth part.
Imagine that.
That fourth part, all the way up and back again.
You earned that one.
The machine sounds like a machine, not a thunderstorm.
I miss the thunder, a little.
Four parts in.
It only wants one more thing, I think. Kindness.
And a part.
Fresh floors, fresh socks.
The ground floor has more house in it than I remembered.
The door downstairs stands open now.
There is more house than there was a while ago.
It's odd, having the ground floor to wander.
It smells of old wood and kitchens.
The ground floor is open to you now.
I've watched it from here for years.
Upstairs is open now.
The stairs are steep, but you are not old yet.
The first floor is open at last.
Mind the little ones' toys, if you visit.
There are beds and wardrobes up on the first floor.
Quite the adventure for a sock.
The first floor, at last.
I remember when the landing creaked in a friendly way.
The attic is open.
Dusty, and full of old things. I fit right in.
Up in the attic now.
The cobwebs have been there longer than me, mind.
The attic is open.
It smells of summers I almost remember.
Something about the attic always made me feel young.
Tall, anyway.
That's it, then. One last wash.
After this, the house is quiet.
The final wash.
I've waited a long time to see this.
Wash well. And well done. All of it.
The machine is mended.
I suppose I owe it an apology. A short one.
There. It's quiet.
I think I miss the rumbling, a little.
Don't tell it.
Mended, at last.
We'll be friends, the washer and I.
After all these winters, it's about time.
I got some presents for you.
